title: Signal-driven capacity routing playbook for enterprise Dedicated requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create an operational playbook used by PMs and Capacity Concierge to turn customer signals (usage patterns, latency targets, budget, compliance requirements) into a deterministic dedicated-capacity proposal: SLA banding, reserved throughput, GPU class recommendation, scaling and burst policies, and fallback model ladder.
background: We receive dozens of enterprise capacity requests per quarter with uneven signal quality. Current reviews are ad hoc and rely heavily on engineering estimation calls. This causes slow onboarding, inconsistent SLA promises, and avoidable cost exposure. The goal of this ticket is to standardize how intake signals map to recommended Dedicated pool configurations so sales/PM/concierge can provide fast, predictable proposals.
scope: Produce a written playbook, a decision matrix spreadsheet, and three templated proposal bundles (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive). Include GPU-family guidance (cost/latency tradeoffs), autoscaling policy templates, and the canonical fallback ladder for model variants.
out_of_scope: Implementing auto-provisioning APIs, changes to pricing or billing engine, or modifying runtime code paths. Those will be separate engineering epics once the playbook is validated.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with example decision flows and a worked example for a chat application with 100k daily active users.
Decision matrix spreadsheet that outputs recommended pool size, GPU family class, and burst credit allocation given input signals.
Three templated customer proposal bundles (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with explicit SLA wording and estimated monthly cost ranges.
Sign-off from Capacity Concierge, Solutions Engineering, and one Enterprise Account Executive.
Two pilot customer reviews performed and feedback incorporated into the playbook.
tasks: Draft intake signal taxonomy (traffic shape, seq length, latency p95/p99 target, compliance, cost sensitivity)
Define SLA bands (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with numeric p99 latency, availability, and throughput guarantees
Map signal ranges to GPU family recommendations (L4 / A10G / A100 / H100), including cost-per-token estimates
Create autoscale templates: headroom-based scaling, queue-length scaler, and scheduled scaling windows
Design fallback ladder: primary production model -> smaller quantized variant -> cross-region model fallback
Assemble templated proposal bundles and sample contract language for reserved throughput
Run two internal runbook reviews with Eng and SRE, then iterate
Publish Confluence doc + attach decision matrix and sample proposals
decisions: Use three SLA bands (Bronze/Silver/Gold) instead of numeric-only thresholds to simplify negotiations and guide GPU class selection
Recommend GPU family by dominant signal (latency-first -> H100/A100, cost-first -> L4/A10G). We will not auto-enforce GPU selection in platform for now.
Reserve throughput measured as 'sequences/sec' for deterministic SLA math; convert from customer RPS using median sequence length assumptions in the matrix.
Burst credits will be offered as a separate line item and decoupled from guaranteed throughput to avoid over-committing capacity.
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs accuracy: SLA bands make sales conversations faster but lose some precision for very unusual workloads
Cost predictability vs utilization: conservative proposals reduce risk of incidents but increase vendor-side idle cost
GPU family guidance avoids forcing hardware choices now; engineering changes required to automate selection later.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft playbook + internal review with Solutions Eng and SRE
Week 2: Create decision matrix and three sample proposals; review with Sales and Legal
Week 3: Run two pilot proposals with existing customer prospects and capture feedback
Week 4: Finalize playbook, publish Confluence page, and add a QuickStart checklist for Concierge team
